solutions.latex:
For $f(x)$: negative gradient, then positive gradient, then negative gradient, then positive gradient.

For $f'(x)$: below the $x$-axis, then above the $x$-axis, then below the $x$-axis, then above the $x$-axis. This matches graph B.

Reading the cumulative frequency polygon at 100, 200 and 300 gives $Q_1=136$, $Q_2$ and $Q_3=172$.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{IQR}&=Q_3-Q_1 \\ &=172-136 \\ &=36 \end{aligned}$$

$(3x)^2+y^2=36$ is a horizontal dilation by a factor of $\tfrac{1}{3}$, so the circle is compressed horizontally, making the left/right extremes at $\pm 2$ now instead of $\pm 6$.

Alternate method: the $x$-intercepts occur when $y=0$.

$$\begin{aligned} (3x)^2+0^2&=36 \\ 9x^2&=36 \\ x^2&=4 \\ x&=\pm 2 \end{aligned}$$

The semicircle has radius 4: $A=\tfrac{1}{2}\pi(4)^2=8\pi$. Each of the four regions below the $x$-axis has signed area $-2$.

$$\begin{aligned} \int_{-8}^{8}f(x)\,dx&=8\pi+(-2\times 4) \\ &=17.13\ldots\approx 17.1 \end{aligned}$$

$y=f(x)$ means substitute $x$-values into $f(x)$ to get $y$-values. $y=g(f(x))$ means substitute $x$ values into $f(x)$, then substitute these $f(x)$ values into $g(x)$, to get the final $y$-values.

Test a point, say when $x=0.5$: $f(x)\approx 0.4$ and $g(f(x))\approx 0.2$. So $y=g(x)$ should include the point $(0.4,0.2)$.

Option A: $x=0.4\to g(x)\approx 0.2$. Option B: $x=0.4\to g(x)\approx 0.001$ (eliminate). Option C: $x=0.4\to g(x)\approx 0.2$. Option D: $x=0.4\to g(x)\approx 0.25$ (eliminate).

Options A and C are left. Test another point, say when $x=-0.5$: $f(x)\approx -0.3$ and $g(f(x))\approx 0.175$. So $y=g(x)$ should include the point $(-0.3,0.175)$.

Option A: $x=-0.3\to g(x)\approx 0.175$. Option C: $x=-0.3\to g(x)\approx -0.001$ (eliminate).

Therefore, Option A must be correct.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{LHS}&=\dfrac{1}{6} \\ \text{RHS}&=\dfrac{2}{3}\times\dfrac{1}{4}=\dfrac{1}{6}=\text{LHS} \end{aligned}$$

or $P(F\cup R)=P(F)+P(R)-P(F\cap R)$:

$$\begin{aligned} \text{LHS}&=\dfrac{3}{4} \\ \text{RHS}&=\dfrac{2}{3}+\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{6}=\dfrac{3}{4}=\text{LHS} \end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} f(x)&=3x^3e^x \\ f'(x)&=3e^x\left(3x^2+x^3\right) \\ f''(x)&=3e^x\left(6x+3x^2\right)+\left(3x^2+x^3\right)3e^x \\ &=18e^xx+9e^xx^2+9e^xx^2+3x^3e^x \\ &=18e^xx+18x^2e^x+3x^3e^x \\ &=3xe^x\left(6+6x+x^2\right) \end{aligned}$$

$f''(x)=0$ for possible points of inflection: $3e^xx\left(x^2+6x+6\right)=0$. Using the null factor law, $3e^x\neq 0$ (no solution since $e^x>0$), $x=0$ or $x^2+6x+6=0$.

$$\begin{aligned} x&=\dfrac{-6\pm\sqrt{36-4(1)6}}{2} \\ &=\dfrac{-6\pm\sqrt{12}}{2} \\ &=-3\pm\sqrt{3} \\ x&=-1.26\ldots,\ x=-4.7\ldots \\ x&=-1.3,\ -4.7 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} f(0)&=3(0)^3e^0=0 \\ f(-1.3)&=-1.7\text{ (to 1 dp)} \\ f(-4.7)&=-2.83\ldots=-2.8\text{ (to 1 dp)} \end{aligned}$$

Possible points of inflection are $(0,0)$, $(-1.3,-1.7)$ and $(-4.7,-2.8)$. Test concavity changes (do not use gradients):

$$\begin{array}{c|cccccccc} x & -5 & -4.7 & -3 & -2 & -1.26 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ \hline f''(x) & -0.1 & 0 & 1.3 & 1.6 & 0 & -0.04 & 0 & 106.0 \end{array}$$

The sign of $f''(x)$ changes ($<0$ to $>0$ about $x=-4.7$, $>0$ to $<0$ about $x=-1.26$, $<0$ to $>0$ about $x=0$), so concavity changes around $x=0,\ -1.3,\ -4.7$.

$\therefore$ Points of inflection $(0,0)$, $(-1.3,-1.7)$ and $(-4.7,-2.8)$.

Stationary points occur when $f'(x)=0$.

$$\begin{aligned} f'(x)&=3e^x\left(3x^2+x^3\right) \\ 3e^x\left(3x^2+x^3\right)&=0 \end{aligned}$$

$3e^x\neq 0$ since $3e^x>0$, no solution; or

$$\begin{aligned} 3x^2+x^3&=0 \\ x^2(3+x)&=0 \\ x^2=0\ &\text{ or }\ 3+x=0 \\ x=0\ &\text{ or }\ x=-3 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} f(0)&=3(0)^3e^0=0 \\ f(-3)&=3(-3)^3e^{-3}=-81e^{-3} \end{aligned}$$

Nature of stationary points:

$$\begin{aligned} f''(x)&=3e^xx\left(6+6x+x^2\right) \\ f''(-3)&=3e^{-3}(-3)\left(6+(6)(-3)+(-3)^2\right) \\ &=27e^{-3} \\ &=1.34>0\quad\text{concave up} \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ minimum turning point at $(-3,-81e^{-3})$.

From part (b), $(0,0)$ is a point of inflection.

$$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ \hline f'(x) & 2.21 & 0 & 32.61 \end{array}$$

The gradient is positive either side of $(0,0)$, so $(0,0)$ is a horizontal point of inflection.

At $x=1$: $y=3(1)^3e^1=3e\approx 8.15$.

$x$-intercept when $y=0$: $0=3x^3e^x$, $e^x\neq 0$, $3x^3=0$, $x=0$. The $y$-intercept is already found, $(0,0)$.

As $x\to-\infty$:

$$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & -6 & -10 & -100 \\ \hline f(x) & -1.6 & -0.14 & -1.1\times 10^{-37} \end{array}$$

Clearly $f(x)\to 0$ from below.
